LESSON: INTERACTIVE SPEAKING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.5: Interactive Speaking
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Interactive Speaking, part of Listening and Speaking in Grade 9 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: Why should we use polite language when interacting with others?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to a conversation on greetings in formal situations,

2. pick out words and phrases used to express greetings in formal contexts e.g. (assalamu alaykum, sabahal khayr, masala khayr, maa ismuka?, keyfa haaluka?” anaa masruurun biliqaika. shukran)

3. respond to formal greetings while applying non-verbal cues (i.e. facing the speaker, maintaining eye contact, gestures, and facial expressions),

4. work jointly to role-play formal greetings in formal settings using non- verbal cues,

5. practise using polite language in a conversation using words (i.e. May I ..., can I borrow your pen please?, “Sorry”, “Excuse me please?”)

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to a conversation on greetings in formal situations,
2. pick out words and phrases used to express greetings in formal contexts e.g. (assalamu alaykum, sabahal khayr, masala khayr, maa ismuka?, keyfa haaluka?” anaa masruurun biliqaika. shukran)
3. respond to formal greetings while applying non-verbal cues (i.e. facing the speaker, maintaining eye contact, gestures, and facial expressions),
4. work jointly to role-play formal greetings in formal settings using non- verbal cues,
5. practise using polite language in a conversation using words (i.e. May I ..., can I borrow your pen please?, “Sorry”, “Excuse me please?”)

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Interactive Speaking together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and Collaboration: This is developed as learner speaks engagingly when responding to formal greetings while

applying non-verbal cues.

Values:
Love: This is portrayed as learner portrays a caring attitude when working jointly to role-play formal greetings in formal settings

using non-verbal cues.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social Cohesion: This is enhanced as learner practises using polite language in a conversation to strengthen unity and respect for

others in the society.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate this concept of greetings to similar concepts of polite language in English.
